dek_candidates: The Mumbai contractor that builds railway platforms, bridges and roads is offering 44,28,000 shares at a price it has not yet set. The filing shows revenue down from ₹90.21 crore to ₹60.53 crore over five years, profit up to ₹3.15 crore in FY2018, and 90.9% of the company still with its promoter.

What A B Infrabuild Limited's DRHP actually discloses: two business segments, a ₹11.30 crore working-capital object, five years of restated numbers in ₹ crore, and the five risks that carry real weight.

The restated statements run most recent period first (FY2018 back to FY2014); state the convention once in the caption rather than re-explaining it per row.

Do not build a peer comparison table with filled cells. Render it as disclosed with the missing labels marked not available, and keep the paragraph that explains why no implied price range is computed.
Cap the risks section at the five listed. Anything further belongs in governance, where the related-party and struck-off-company facts already sit.
Explain the tender process before using the words 'order book', so the reader understands an order book is a stack of cancellable contracts, not a revenue forecast.
Use the ₹90.21 crore to ₹60.53 crore revenue fall against the ₹3.15 crore FY2018 profit as the spine of the piece; return to it in the financials section with the actual five-year series.
No verdict on the offer. The filing states what it states; the reader decides.

beats.beat: The filing describes two segments: creation of infrastructure, and operating a ready mix concrete plant.

Infrastructure here is three named kinds of work: railways (designing and constructing platforms and station buildings, gauge conversion, laying track), bridges (beam, cantilever, arch, suspension, cable-stayed and truss), and roadways (bituminous and concrete roads linking highways and district roads).

The second segment is a single physical asset: a ready mix concrete facility at Kashimira in Thane district, Maharashtra, described in the filing as the company's state of the art facility and advanced machinery.

Work is won by tender, and the filing sets out the six steps: the client floats a tender, a pre-bid meeting settles queries, the contractor bids, the job goes to the lowest quote with a Letter of Acceptance, the contractor deposits a performance guarantee, then drawings are issued and the site handed over.

Explain what 'lowest quote wins' means commercially — the bidder who wins is the bidder who has agreed to the thinnest margin, so the ability to estimate cost accurately is the business, and the filing separately warns that contracts can turn to losses if costs rise above estimates.

The named customer list is dominated by public bodies: Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd, Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority, Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd — alongside private names including Sky Way Infrastructure Private Limited, Dev Engineers, GCC Hotel Private Ltd and Krypton Corp.
Western Railway has been a client since 2006, which is the longest relationship the filing claims.

Concentration is the defining feature of the order book: Western Railway accounts for 52% of orders on hand, and Indian Railways as a whole was the largest customer at 57% of revenue in Fiscal 2018 — the same 57% figure the filing uses for revenue from key customers for the period ended March 31, 2018.

The footprint is narrow on purpose: the filing calls the company a major player in developing infrastructure in the city of Mumbai, consolidating in Maharashtra with a strong order book. It does not disclose a segment-wise revenue split between infrastructure and ready mix concrete, or a plant or headcount figure beyond the one Thane facility.
The promoter and the senior team are described as having more than 20 years in the infrastructure industry, and the filing claims box pushing as a technique the company uses on its projects.

beats.beat: Set the convention for the reader: the restated statements present five periods, and the excerpt's column order runs most recent first, FY2018 back to FY2014 — the filing's own trend notes on revenue and profit confirm the mapping. All figures below are converted from lakhs to ₹ crore by dividing by 100.

Revenue from operations over five years: ₹86.61 crore (FY2014), ₹90.21 crore (FY2015), ₹74.53 crore (FY2016), ₹73.44 crore (FY2017), ₹60.53 crore (FY2018). The top line has fallen by roughly a third from its FY2015 peak.

Restated net profit after adjustments over the same five years: ₹0.96 crore (FY2014), ₹0.78 crore (FY2015), ₹0.33 crore (FY2016), ₹0.16 crore (FY2017), ₹3.15 crore (FY2018). The filing flags the FY2018 jump explicitly as a sharp increase from ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017.

Profit before interest, depreciation and tax, which is the closest thing to EBITDA the restated statements give: ₹7.84 crore (FY2014), ₹9.46 crore (FY2015), ₹7.83 crore (FY2016), ₹6.76 crore (FY2017), ₹9.29 crore (FY2018) — a swing back up in FY2018 on a smaller revenue base, which is the single most interesting line in the filing.
Total assets rose from ₹70.62 crore (FY2014) to ₹82.32 crore (FY2018), with a dip to ₹62.95 crore in FY2016.

The debt mix has flipped. Long term borrowings fell from ₹6.73 crore in FY2015 to ₹1.33 crore in FY2018, while short term borrowings rose from ₹30.82 crore in FY2014 to ₹35.37 crore in FY2018 — so the company now runs almost entirely on short-dated money, roughly ₹35.37 crore against ₹60.53 crore of FY2018 revenue.

The filing states the company had negative cash flow in recent financial years and warns that sustained negative cash flow could adversely affect business, financial condition and results. The excerpts do not give the cash flow statement's line items, so the size of the negative figure cannot be reported.

Liquidity pressure on top of that: ₹405.02 lakhs (₹4.05 crore) of unsecured loans outstanding as on March 31, 2018, repayable on demand, where any demand for repayment may affect cash flow and financial condition.

And the collection side: the filing warns that failure to recover amounts from sundry debtors and trade receivables in a timely manner might affect financial condition — which is the mechanism by which a profitable year can still produce negative cash.

beats.beat: One person owns almost the whole company. Promoter Amit Bholanath Mishra holds 74,95,476 equity shares, or 90.949% of pre-issue paid-up capital, with PAN AAMPM3121G.

Explain what 90.949% pre-issue means for a buyer: after the offer the promoter still holds the overwhelming majority, so public shareholders are a minority with no practical ability to influence decisions, and the filing does not disclose a post-issue holding figure.

The other directors hold nominal stakes — Bharat kumar Parmar, Shree Prakash Singh and Mukesh Pandey each hold 300 equity shares — while Key Management Personnel Hatim Sakerwala holds 9% of the equity shares as on the date of the draft.

The two named key management personnel are young relative to their roles: Ms. Anchal Pachori, 28, a Chartered Accountant, is Chief Financial Officer and head of accounts and finance, and Mr. Mohit Soni, 26, an Associate Member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, is Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. This is a statement of the disclosure, not a criticism.

On the clean-record side, the filing states none of the directors is on the RBI list of willful defaulters, there have been no criminal cases or investigations against any director, and the promoter has confirmed he has not been declared a willful defaulter — while separately disclosing that the company, its promoter and its directors are involved in litigation pending at various stages.

Related-party money movements the filing quantifies for FY2018: loans taken from key managerial personnel or the board of ₹68.4 lakhs, director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs, and outstanding payables to related parties of ₹324.3 lakhs as on 31.03.2018.
The filing concedes the pattern can continue: it has entered into related party transactions in the past and may do so in the future.

Two companies promoted by the promoter were struck off by the Registrar of Companies for non-operation of business — Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited on March 12, 2016 and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited on March 11, 2016.

Two controls are absent by the filing's own admission: no independent agency was appointed to appraise the proposed project, and no monitoring agency was appointed, so deployment of the issue proceeds sits with management and the board, monitored only by the audit committee.

governance.heading: Who controls it

beats.beat: The filing places the company in infrastructure and construction, defined there as power, bridges, dams, roads and urban infrastructure development.

That market is described as highly fragmented and working capital intensive, contributing roughly 8% of India's GDP at constant prices — fragmentation matters because it means no single contractor sets price.
The demand case rests on a spending number: India needs infrastructure investment worth ₹50 trillion (US$777.73 billion) by 2022 for sustainable development.

Government programmes are named as the demand drivers — 100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India and Power for All — with FDI norms eased in 15 sectors including real estate and construction development.
Foreign money into the sector is sized at US$24.67 billion between April 2000 and December 2017.

The macro backdrop the filing cites: cumulative growth in the index of eight core industries was 4.2% in 2017-18, India's GDP growth stayed above 7% in 2017, and India moved up 19 places to rank 35th of 160 countries on the World Bank's 2016 Logistics Performance Index.

On competition the filing is qualitative and admits the company competes with firms in both the organised and the unorganised sector. No competitor is named anywhere in the excerpts, so the report cannot build a named competitive set.

The three headwinds the filing lists for itself: a slow pace of government projects, a working capital crunch that may affect profitability, and changes in government policies. Explain why the first is the sharpest — the company's customers are the government, so the government's pace of awarding and paying is the company's revenue cycle.

Regulatory context that touches the business directly: the Companies Act, 2013 governs the company, GST applies to supply of goods and services, the Factories Act, 1948 regulates labour in factories, and environmental legislation including the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974, the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1981 and the Environment Protection Act 1986 applies to operations.

industry.heading: The market it sells into

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is a Mumbai-based infrastructure contractor that builds for the railways and roads departments and also runs a ready-mix concrete plant — it does two things, not one, and the filing splits its business that way.

The offer is 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 face value each, at a price that is left blank in the filing — the DRHP prints the issue price as ₹[•], so no price band and no implied valuation can be taken from it.
The money raised has two named destinations: ₹1,130 lakhs (₹11.30 crore) for working capital, and general corporate purposes, for which the filing does not disclose an amount.

The tension in this filing is that the top line and the bottom line move in opposite directions: revenue fell from ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018, while restated profit after tax rose from ₹0.78 crore in FY2015 to ₹3.15 crore in FY2018.
Explain in two sentences what a DRHP is and why the price is blank at this stage — the document is filed before the price is set, so everything here is an estimate of scale, not a valuation.

intro.purpose: Orient a first-time reader: what A B Infrabuild is, what it is selling, and the one contrast that defines the filing.

beats.beat: The offer is 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at an issue price to be determined.
Explain face value versus issue price in a clause: ₹10 is the accounting denomination of the share, while the issue price is what a buyer pays on top of it, and the filing prints that as ₹[•].
The objects of the issue are named: ₹1,130 lakhs (₹11.30 crore) to meet working capital requirements, and general corporate purposes, where the amount is left as [x] and is not disclosed.

Explain why a contractor needs the working capital first: the same six-step tender process requires a performance guarantee before a site is handed over, and public-sector clients pay on their own cycle — so growth consumes cash before it produces it. The filing itself confirms the company had negative cash flow in recent financial years.
The intermediaries named in the filing are the Lead Manager, Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited, and the Registrar to the Issue, Bigshare Services Private Limited.

State plainly what the excerpts do not establish: whether the 44,28,000 shares are entirely a fresh issue, whether any part is an offer for sale, and the identity of any selling shareholder. Nothing in the available pages answers it.

offer.heading: The offer and what the money is for
offer.purpose: Set out the share count, the objects, and the intermediaries — and be explicit about what the filing has left blank.

beats.beat: Customer concentration. Indian Railways was the largest customer at 57% of revenue in Fiscal 2018, and Western Railway alone is 52% of orders on hand — the filing states that losing Indian Railways as its largest customer would cause a significant dip in revenue.

Winning new work is not in the company's hands. Revenue depends on government departments accepting its bids, and its attempts to secure government and PSU projects may not always succeed — a failure to obtain new contracts would materially and adversely affect its financial condition.

Negative cash flow. The company had negative cash flow in recent financial years, and the filing warns that sustained negative cash flow could adversely affect the business, financial condition and results.

Receivables and demand loans. Slow recovery of sundry debtors and trade receivables could hurt financial condition, and ₹405.02 lakhs of unsecured loans were outstanding as on March 31, 2018, repayable on demand — money that can be called at any time.

The promoter's other companies and related-party flows. Two promoter companies were struck off by the ROC in March 2016 for non-operation, and the filing says related-party transactions have occurred and may continue — in FY2018 alone, ₹68.4 lakhs of loans from key managerial personnel or the board, ₹57.7 lakhs of director remuneration and ₹324.3 lakhs of outstanding payables to related parties.

risks.heading: Five risks that carry weight
risks.purpose: Give the reader the five company-specific risks the filing itself ranks highest, each with the number or the mechanism attached.

beats.beat: The issue price is printed as ₹[●], and the filing states only that it will be [●] times the ₹10 face value. Without a price there is no issuer P/E to compare with anything.

The filing does contain a section headed Comparison of Accounting Ratios with Peer Group Companies, on which it states the issue price is justified, and the numbers 12.39, 44.71, 28.14, 6053.05 and 10 appear in the excerpt from that page — but the digest does not preserve the peer names or which figure belongs to which column.

Explain the arithmetic the brief asked for and why it cannot be done: applying a peer multiple requires a peer P/E and an issuer earnings-per-share. Neither is attributable from the excerpt, and the issue price itself is redacted, so no implied price range is computed here — that is a limit of the disclosure, not a judgment about the offer.

The filing also tabulates per-year accounting ratios for the three most recent periods. The values shown include 4.14, 1.97 and 28.14 for the years ended March 31, 2016, 2017 and 2018 respectively, and a second set of 1.31, 0.63 and 12.59 — but the excerpt does not label which ratio each column represents, so no ratio should be named in the report beyond quoting the numbers as printed.
One pricing-adjacent disclosure the reader should hold: the company issued equity shares in the twelve months before the filing at a price which may be lower than the issue price.

valuation_and_peers.heading: What the filing says about pricing
valuation_and_peers.purpose: Report honestly that the two inputs needed for a peer-multiple valuation — an issue price and an attributable peer set — are not available in the excerpts, and say exactly why.
